statement: Markup is lean and minimal: few divs, classes, scripts, inline styles and meta tags, with no external stylesheets.
Heading hierarchy is clean and properly nested: a single h1, h2 section titles, h3 for cards or items, and h4 for footer or sub-groups.
Images carry descriptive alt text.
Header is compact with a small logo and single-row navigation/links alongside it.
Content sits in a centered, constrained/max-width container with generous side margins/gutters rather than running full width.
Content is arranged in multi-column grids of equal-sized cards (rows of cards, often bordered, with arrows, icons or images).
Layout is built with CSS grid and flexbox.
Page uses semantic landmark elements (e.g., header, nav, main, section, footer, aside) to structure content.
Page title combines the brand name with a descriptive tagline (e.g., separated by a pipe, dash, or em dash) rather than being a bare brand or keyword string.
Cards are defined by thin borders and rounded corners rather than shadows or fills.
Small uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow/kicker labels sit above section headings or titles.
Body text is slightly larger (about 17px) with generous line height (about 1.6–1.65).
Uses semantic landmark and sectioning elements (header, main, footer, section, nav, article, aside), along with a clean heading outline.
Corners are generously rounded (roughly 8–16px radii on cards and inputs), with pill shapes on buttons, chips and badges.
Typography relies solely on a system-ui font stack, with no web fonts or icon fonts.
Page is self-contained: inline styles in a single style block, with no external scripts or stylesheets.
Images carry descriptive alt text for meaningful images and empty alt for decorative icons or thumbnails.
Page title is a short, brand-only or organization-only name without subtitle or keyword stuffing.
Page has exactly one h1 containing the hero headline, with a clear heading hierarchy.
Typography pairs a serif face (Georgia) for headings with a sans-serif (system/Helvetica) for body and UI text.
Buttons are fully rounded pills, in filled primary and outlined secondary variants.
Uses a generic system sans-serif font stack (system-ui/Helvetica Neue/Arial) rather than a custom web font or the browser default serif.
Body text uses a generous, relaxed line height of about 1.55–1.6 on a 16px base.
Palette is a navy/dark-blue scheme with blue and white, plus bright or warm accent colors (amber, yellow, red, magenta, brick-red).
Links end with a right-arrow glyph (→) as a trailing affordance, such as 'View all' or 'More →' links.
Footer is a multi-column directory with uppercase letter-spaced headings and plain text links, with a bottom bar below a divider.
Layout uses CSS grid and flexbox within a narrower centered content container.
Hero is a two-column split with text on one side and a single photo/image on the other.
Page background is a warm off-white cream rather than pure white or black.
Flat styling with no box shadows, gradients or animations.
Footer is dark navy or dark with light text and white column headings in multiple columns.
Page is compact and short, with few sections, less content, and tighter spacing.
Page uses a dark theme with dark navy/near-black background and near-white text.
Hero background is a gradient (e.g., navy or blue to cyan) with prominent white headline text over it.
Announcement appears as a full-width colored strip (rather than a modal box), sometimes with a badge or underlined link.
Primary call-to-action buttons are fully rounded pills in an accent color (e.g. yellow with dark navy text).
Section headings (h2) are bold rather than light weight, and left-aligned/large.
Social links are plain text labels with no icons or icon glyphs; header and footer use text-only links.
Defines many CSS transitions/hover effects for interactive states, giving subtle polish.
Part of the hero headline is highlighted in an accent color while the rest stays in a contrasting color.
Rounded corners and large radii are applied widely across cards, buttons and containers.
Section headings carry a short accent underline bar beneath the text (e.g., orange or yellow).
Sections alternate between dark navy and light (white/grey/pale) background bands.
Badges (e.g. review counts, 'TRENDING', 'NEW!') are rendered as small accent-colored pill-shaped labels.
A single warm orange or orange-red accent color is used for CTAs, links, labels, badges, underlines and borders.
Head includes charset, viewport and description meta tags.
Text-only cards are white cards with an accent-colored left border.
Copy uses typographic (curly) apostrophes/quotes and dashes rather than straight ones.
Sections alternate between white and pale blue-gray/tinted background bands, with a dark navy footer.
Footer is a dark band with a divider rule above a copyright line, alongside logo/links or extended link columns.
Layout is a single-column stack of full-width sections, each with centered content, with no sidebar.
Icons are plain text glyphs or characters (arrows, ☰) rather than SVG, image, sprite, or icon-font icons.
Palette is built on green/teal: a saturated green or teal accent, mint tints, and dark green or slate text (sometimes with mustard and cream).
Photo/artwork backgrounds are darkened or overlaid with dark tints, with white text on top.
